  "id": "p_002",
  "summary": "A minimal single-resource Task REST API specified as an OpenAPI 3.1 JSON document: five endpoints, a seven-field task model, and uniform RFC 9457-style error responses.",
  "approach": "Model the Tasks API as one collection at /tasks. Use GET to list, GET /{id} to fetch, POST to create, PATCH /{id} to partially update, and DELETE /{id} to remove. Server generates id, createdAt, and updatedAt; clients never send them. Use application/json everywhere, a data envelope for successful payloads, and a compact RFC 9457-style error object for failures. Express the whole contract as machine-readable OpenAPI JSON, with schemas, examples, and status codes.",
  "tradeoffs": [
    "PATCH rather than PUT avoids full replacement payloads but requires clients and servers to treat all fields as optional.",
    "A data envelope gives response extensibility but adds wrapping compared with a bare resource array/object.",
    "Rejecting unknown fields is stricter and prevents silent typos but can be less forgiving for exploratory clients.",
    "No pagination/filtering/sorting keeps the surface minimal but limits usability if task count grows."
  ],
  "evidence": [
    "OpenAPI 3.1 is the OAS standard for describing REST APIs; JSON Schema 2020-12 is used for request/response bodies.",
    "PATCH is an established HTTP method for partial resource modification (RFC 5789).",
    "RFC 3339 date-time and RFC 4122 UUID are the conventional formats for timestamps and identifiers.",
    "RFC 9457 defines a standard, machine-readable JSON error format used by the API."
  ],
